abstract: Traditional livestock breeds are reservoirs of genetic variation lost elsewhere by selection for productivity, yet are rarely represented in reference genome resources. Traditional cattle (Bos taurus) in the Netherlands are severely endangered, with some populations having declined by up to 95 % between 2020 and 2026. We generated 12 assemblies from seven traditional Dutch breeds and combined them with a Holstein Friesian assembly and the Hereford cattle reference to build the first Dutch cattle pangenome (2 881 293 997 bp), a graph containing 193.4 Mb of sequence absent from the international reference. More than 80 % of this sequence was breed private, and this fraction rose with variant size to 99 % for segments of at least one kilobase. Genotyping 54 short-read sequenced animals of these Dutch breeds against the graph recovered 55 865 structural variants and resolved four genetic clusters. The Groningen White Headed was the most differentiated breed while carrying the lowest nucleotide diversity, whereas the recently derived Improved Red and Deep Red remained close to their Meuse-Rhine-Yssel progenitor. Holstein Friesian formed no cluster of its own and contributed the least amount of novel sequence, a reflection of its historical use in upgrading traditional breeds. Ten structural variants located within genes were fixed within a single breed and ranked among the most breed-differentiated of all 55 865 SVs by VST , including a 174 bp deletion in KIT in the Dutch Belted. Pangenomes recover breed-defining variation that linear references cannot represent, supporting conservation and selection in traditional cattle.
